The writer uses specific sensory details, particularly relating to sight and touch, to create a vivid and believable scene. For example, the reader is introduced to the temperature of the environment with the mention of the "große Hitze des Tages" (great heat of the day). Visually, the characters are described in rich detail: Herr von Bülow is pictured slouching with his legs stretched out, one hand in his pocket, and the other gesturing wildly in the air, while Herr Sander is contrasted by his "schwarzer Vollbart" (full black beard), a tight coat of "niederländischem Tuche" (Dutch cloth) constricting his stoutness, and his "feinste weiße Wäsche" (finest white linen). Finally, the author effectively uses light and shadow at the end of the excerpt, describing Victoire leaning out from the shadows into the "Lichtschein der Lampe" (glow of the lamp), which illuminates her fine profile and the texture of her "Blatternarben" (pockmarks). These details make the salon setting and its inhabitants feel tangible and real.
